Apple___Apple_scab.description: Produces olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit, causing premature defoliation and fruit deformities.
cultural_controls: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering fungal spores.
Prune canopy during dormancy to promote rapid leaf drying and air circulation.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
chemical_controls: Apply protective fungicides (Captan, Mancozeb) at bud break and early bloom.
Use systemic fungicides (Myclobutanil, Difenoconazole) if post-infection control is required.
biological_controls: Apply sulfur-based organic sprays or liquid copper at green tip stage.
Foliar applications of Bacillus subtilis or potassium bicarbonate.
preventive_measures: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Enterprise, Freedom).
Apply 5% urea spray in late autumn to accelerate leaf decomposition.

severity_actions.Mild: Remove affected leaves manually, monitor weather for rain periods, and apply preventive bio-fungicide.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply targeted fungicide (Captan or Myclobutanil) immediately; ensure complete canopy coverage.
severity_actions.Severe: Initiate full systemic fungicide schedule every 7-10 days, prune heavily infected shoots, and inspect fruit clusters.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Causes small purple specks that enlarge into frogeye leaf spots with light brown centers and purple margins, limb cankers, and fruit rot.
cultural_controls: Prune out dead wood, fire blight strikes, and mummified fruit which harbor inoculum.
Maintain tree vigor through balanced fertilization and proper irrigation.
chemical_controls: Apply fungicides containing Captan, Mancozeb, or Thiophanate-methyl from pink bud through petal fall.
biological_controls: Apply copper sprays during delayed dormant period.
Use bio-fungicides such as Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
preventive_measures: Sanitize pruning tools between cuts with 70% alcohol.
Avoid bark injury during mowing and equipment operations.

severity_actions.Mild: Prune out visible cankers and remove spotted leaves; apply protective copper spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Captan or Thiophanate-methyl spray; remove all infected fruit mummies from branches and ground.
severity_actions.Severe: Excise infected branch cankers 6-8 inches below visible lesion; apply systemic fungicide program.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Bright orange-yellow circular spots appear on leaves in spring, developing tiny raised pustules and tube-like structures on the underside.
cultural_controls: Remove nearby Eastern Red Cedar and juniper trees (alternate hosts) within 1-2 miles if feasible.
Prune gall swellings on ornamental junipers before orange spore horns emerge in spring.
chemical_controls: Apply Myclobutanil, Propiconazole, or Mancozeb from pink bud stage through early summer.
biological_controls: Sulfur sprays applied before anticipated rain events during primary infection periods.
preventive_measures: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties (e.g., Redfree, Liberty, William's Pride).

severity_actions.Mild: Monitor neighboring juniper hosts; apply preventive bio-sulfur spray during wet spring spells.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Myclobutanil or Mancozeb fungicide spray to prevent leaf drop.
severity_actions.Severe: Full protective fungicide coverage every 7-10 days until cedar spore release subsides.

Apple___healthy.description: Leaf foliage is healthy, showing vibrant green pigmentation, intact leaf structure, and no visible lesions.
cultural_controls: Maintain regular drip irrigation and balanced seasonal fertilization (N-P-K + micronutrients).
Perform annual structural pruning to maintain airflow and sunlight penetration.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required. Continue routine pest monitoring.
biological_controls: Encourage beneficial predatory insects and pollinators.
preventive_measures: Conduct bi-weekly visual inspections during peak growing season.
Maintain clean orchard floor and mulching.

severity_actions.Healthy: No treatment required. Maintain current orchard management and preventive scouting.

Blueberry___healthy.description: Foliage exhibits vigorous growth, deep green color, and absence of chlorosis or fungal spots.
cultural_controls: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 - 5.5) using elemental sulfur or peat moss.
Apply organic pine bark or sawdust mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Maintain mycorrhizal soil health.
preventive_measures: Regular soil moisture monitoring and acidifying irrigation water if alkaline.

severity_actions.Healthy: No treatment needed. Maintain optimal acidic soil and mulch depth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: White powdery fungal patches on the surface of young leaves, causing leaf curling, distortion, and stunted shoot growth.
cultural_controls: Prune to increase sunlight and canopy ventilation.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which stimulates overly susceptible succulent growth.
chemical_controls: Apply Quinoxyfen, Triflumizole, or Myclobutanil at petal fall and shuck fall stages.
biological_controls: Potassium bicarbonate (Armicarb/Kaligreen) or horticultural neem oil.
Foliar sulfur sprays during early season.
preventive_measures: Scout young shoots at the base and interior of trees regularly.

severity_actions.Mild: Apply potassium bicarbonate or horticultural oil; prune infected water sprouts.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply targeted powdery mildew fungicide (Myclobutanil or Triflumizole).
severity_actions.Severe: Rotate between FRAC group 3 and 11 fungicides every 10-14 days to prevent resistance.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Leaves are robust, glossy green, and free of spots, shot holes, or mildew.
cultural_controls: Maintain consistent soil moisture, especially during fruit sizing.
Apply organic mulch around drip line.
chemical_controls: None needed.
biological_controls: Preserve natural beneficial insect populations.
preventive_measures: Conduct regular canopy scouting for cherry fruit fly and fungal leaf spot.

severity_actions.Healthy: Healthy canopy. Maintain standard orchard sanitation and irrigation.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Rectangular, brown to gray lesions delimited by leaf veins, spreading from lower canopy upward in warm, humid weather.
cultural_controls: Rotate crops away from corn for at least 1-2 years.
Utilize conventional tillage to bury crop debris where feasible.
chemical_controls: Apply strobilurin and triazole premix fungicides (Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad, Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole) at VT-R1 growth stage.
biological_controls: Bio-fungicides like Bacillus subtilis applied early in disease development.
preventive_measures: Select corn hybrids with high Gray Leaf Spot tolerance ratings.

severity_actions.Mild: Monitor disease progression toward the ear leaf; evaluate economic threshold.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply dual-mode-of-action fungicide at VT/R1 tassel stage.
severity_actions.Severe: Immediate fungicide application to protect upper canopy and ear leaves; plan 2-year crop rotation.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Small, powdery, cinnamon-brown circular to elongate pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
cultural_controls: Plant early in the season to escape peak wind-borne airborne spore loads.
chemical_controls: Fungicides containing Azoxystrobin, Pyraclostrobin, or Tebuconazole if rust appears prior to tasseling on susceptible hybrids.
biological_controls: Sulfur dust or neem-based antifungal formulations in organic farming.
preventive_measures: Plant corn hybrids with Rp-gene resistance.

severity_actions.Mild: Scout field weekly; rust rarely requires treatment if appearing late in grain fill.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply foliar fungicide if lesions appear on upper leaves 2 weeks before tasseling.
severity_actions.Severe: Spray systemic triazole/strobilurin mix immediately to protect grain yield.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (1-6 inches long) that rapidly coalesce and kill leaf tissue.
cultural_controls: Crop rotation with non-host crops (soybean, small grains).
Manage crop residue to accelerate degradation.
chemical_controls: Apply strobilurin/triazole combination fungicides (Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole, Pyraclostrobin + Metconazole).
biological_controls: Trichoderma-based biocontrol products applied early.
preventive_measures: Select resistant hybrids with multi-gene resistance (Ht1, Ht2, Ht3).

severity_actions.Mild: Monitor lower leaves; scout field every 5 days during wet, overcast weather.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply fungicide before silking if lesions reach the third leaf below the ear.
severity_actions.Severe: Immediate systemic fungicide spray; ensure high pressure and spray volume for deep canopy penetration.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Vibrant, clean green foliage with no rust pustules, cigar lesions, or fungal spotting.
cultural_controls: Ensure balanced soil nutrition (proper N sidedressing at V6).
Maintain appropriate plant population density.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Promote beneficial soil microbiology.
preventive_measures: Continue routine crop scouting through reproductive stages.

severity_actions.Healthy: Crop is in optimal health. Continue standard agronomic management.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Small circular reddish-brown leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black pycnidia; causes grape berries to shrivel into hard black mummies.
cultural_controls: Canopy management: shoot thinning, leaf pulling, and trellis training for rapid drying.
Remove and destroy all mummified fruit clusters during winter pruning.
chemical_controls: Apply Mancozeb, Captan, or Myclobutanil starting at bud break (1-inch shoot growth) through 4 weeks post-bloom.
biological_controls: Copper hydroxide or liquid lime sulfur during early shoot development.
preventive_measures: Maintain weed-free zone under vine rows to enhance ground airflow.

severity_actions.Mild: Remove affected leaves and shoot tips; apply protective Mancozeb spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply systemic Myclobutanil or Difenoconazole; remove all diseased fruit clusters.
severity_actions.Severe: Implement intensive 7-day spray rotation until veraison; prune severely damaged canes.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Causes tiger-stripe chlorotic and necrotic patterns between leaf veins, dark spot speckling on berries, and sudden apoplexy collapse.
cultural_controls: Practice delayed pruning (late winter) to reduce spore infection of pruning wounds.
Seal all large pruning wounds (>1 inch diameter) with wound sealant or pruning paint.
chemical_controls: Apply wound protectant fungicides (Thiophanate-methyl) directly to fresh pruning cuts.
biological_controls: Apply Trichoderma-based bio-protectants (e.g., Trichoderma atroviride) immediately after pruning.
preventive_measures: Avoid cutting into old infected wood; sanitize pruning shears with 10% bleach or alcohol.

severity_actions.Mild: Mark infected vines for selective winter sanitation; protect all pruning wounds with sealant.
severity_actions.Moderate: Excise infected cordons below visible wood necrosis; apply Trichoderma protectant.
severity_actions.Severe: Retrain a new healthy sucker from base or replace vine; properly dispose of infected trunks.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Large, irregular brown to dark red necrotic spots on mature leaves, leading to yellowing, premature leaf drop, and weakened vines.
cultural_controls: Prune excess foliage in the fruit zone to improve airflow.
Collect and destroy infected autumn leaf litter.
chemical_controls: Apply Copper oxychloride, Mancozeb, or Pyraclostrobin post-harvest or at first symptom emergence.
biological_controls: Bordeaux mixture or copper soaps.
Bacillus subtilis foliar sprays.
preventive_measures: Avoid excess overhead irrigation that prolongs leaf wetness.

severity_actions.Mild: Rake fallen leaves, improve trellis aeration, and apply copper fungicide spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Mancozeb or Strobilurin fungicide; ensure coverage of lower and inner leaf surfaces.
severity_actions.Severe: Full vineyard fungicide coverage; strip severely defoliated shoots and burn debris.

Grape___healthy.description: Vine leaves are clean, broad, and uniform deep green without chlorosis, spots, or powdery residue.
cultural_controls: Maintain proper shoot positioning and trellis wire tension.
Regulate irrigation using drip systems to prevent water stress.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Support beneficial predatory mites for natural pest management.
preventive_measures: Routine weekly scouting for early signs of downy/powdery mildew and black rot.

severity_actions.Healthy: Vines are healthy. Continue standard viticulture canopy and nutrition practices.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen_type: Bacterial (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, vectored by Asian Citrus Psyllid)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle leaf yellowing, yellow veins, small lopsided bitter green fruit, and progressive dieback of tree canopy.
cultural_controls: Inspect orchard for Asian Citrus Psyllid vectors (Diaphorina citri).
Remove and destroy PCR-confirmed infected trees immediately to reduce inoculum source.
chemical_controls: Control psyllid vectors with rotational insecticides (Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam, Fenpropathrin).
Apply foliar nutritional sprays (Zinc, Manganese, Boron) to sustain tree production.
biological_controls: Release Tamarixia radiata parasitoid wasps for biological psyllid suppression.
preventive_measures: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock from screenhouses.
Establish physical protective windbreaks or screen barriers.

severity_actions.Mild: Isolate tree, treat immediately for psyllid vectors with systemic insecticide, submit tissue for PCR testing.
severity_actions.Moderate: Intensive vector suppression; apply enhanced micronutrient foliar program to alleviate symptoms.
severity_actions.Severe: Eradicate and burn infected tree to prevent vector transmission to neighboring healthy citrus blocks.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Small water-soaked angular spots on leaves turning purple-brown, centers drop out giving a shot-hole appearance; causes severe defoliation and fruit pitting.
cultural_controls: Avoid planting in excessively sandy, wind-exposed sites without windbreaks.
Avoid heavy summer nitrogen applications which stimulate late susceptible growth.
chemical_controls: Apply copper bactericides during dormant and bud-swell stages.
Apply Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) sprays during bloom and petal fall.
biological_controls: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or bacteriophage products.
preventive_measures: Select resistant peach cultivars (e.g., Redhaven, Candor, Biscoe).

severity_actions.Mild: Apply low-rate copper or bio-bactericide spray; minimize foliage abrasion from wind.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Oxytetracycline or copper-mancozeb tank mix every 7 days during wet weather.
severity_actions.Severe: Full bactericide schedule; prune affected twigs during dormancy; improve windbreak protection.

Peach___healthy.description: Foliage is lanceolate, smooth, glossy green, and free of shot-holes, cankers, or curl.
cultural_controls: Prune into open-center vase structure to allow maximum light penetration.
Maintain proper soil drainage to prevent root rot.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Maintain orchard ground cover to support beneficial insects.
preventive_measures: Dormant copper spray in late winter to prevent peach leaf curl.

severity_actions.Healthy: Healthy foliage. Continue standard stone-fruit nutrition and orchard management.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Small, water-soaked circular to irregular dark brown spots with yellow halos on leaves, causing widespread blighting and leaf shedding.
cultural_controls: Use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers to keep foliage dry.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Sanitize stakes, trays, and tools.
chemical_controls: Apply fixed copper tank-mixed with Mancozeb (improves copper solubility and bacterial kill).
biological_controls: Foliar sprays of Bacillus subtilis, Streptomyces lydicus, or copper soap formulations.
preventive_measures: Plant certified disease-free, hot-water-treated seed or resistant hybrid pepper varieties.

severity_actions.Mild: Remove infected lower leaves; apply copper-mancozeb or Bacillus spray; avoid working in wet fields.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply copper + mancozeb bactericide every 5-7 days; strictly avoid overhead watering.
severity_actions.Severe: Intensive bactericide program; rogue out severely infected plants; sanitize all harvesting tools.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Leaves are crisp, deep green, and free of blemishes, chlorosis, or bacterial spotting.
cultural_controls: Provide consistent moisture through drip lines and balanced fertilization (calcium prevents blossom end rot).
Mulch soil bed with plastic or straw.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Deploy beneficial insectary plants (alyssum, dill) nearby.
preventive_measures: Monitor underside of leaves for aphids and thrips.

severity_actions.Healthy: Healthy crop. Maintain consistent soil moisture and nutrient fertigation.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Characteristic brown to black target-board lesions with concentric rings, surrounded by yellow chlorotic margins on mature leaves.
cultural_controls: Avoid overhead irrigation; schedule watering early in the morning.
Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium fertility (stressed plants are more susceptible).
Rotate crops away from potatoes and tomatoes for 3 years.
chemical_controls: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at initial symptom detection.
biological_controls: Foliar bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis, copper octanoate).
preventive_measures: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers.
Destroy potato cull piles before planting season.

severity_actions.Mild: Strip lower infected leaves; apply protective Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply systemic fungicide (Azoxystrobin or Boscalid); ensure thorough canopy penetration.
severity_actions.Severe: Spray dual-action fungicide every 7 days; protect tubers by maintaining soil hilling.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Rapidly expanding water-soaked dark green to purplish-black lesions with white fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in humid conditions; can destroy entire fields in days.
cultural_controls: Destroy all volunteer potato plants and cull piles.
Ensure deep hill covering over tubers to prevent spore washdown.
Never irrigate in the late afternoon or evening.
chemical_controls: Apply specialized oomycete fungicides: Mandipropamid, Cymoxanil, Fluopicolide, or Chlorothalonil.
biological_controls: Fixed copper hydroxide sprays applied preventively.
preventive_measures: Plant certified blight-resistant seed potatoes; subscribe to local blight forecasting warnings.

severity_actions.Mild: Apply translaminar fungicide (Cymoxanil + Mancozeb) immediately; alert surrounding growers.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply systemic anti-oomycete fungicide (Mandipropamid/Fluopicolide) on strict 5-day cycle.
severity_actions.Severe: Desiccate / vine-kill canopy before harvest to prevent spore washdown and tuber rotting; do not harvest wet tubers.

Potato___healthy.description: Leaves are broad, healthy dark green, with vigorous vine development and clean leaf surfaces.
cultural_controls: Maintain adequate soil hilling to cover growing tubers from sunlight and blight spores.
Balanced irrigation to avoid drought or waterlogging.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Promote healthy soil rhizosphere.
preventive_measures: Conduct regular scouting for Colorado potato beetles and early blight symptoms.

severity_actions.Healthy: Potato canopy is thriving. Continue standard hilling, irrigation, and scouting.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Canes and leaves show bright green serrated foliage, healthy primocanes, and no rust or cane blight.
cultural_controls: Prune floricanes to the ground immediately after harvest.
Trellis canes to maintain upright growth and airflow.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Mulch root zone with wood chips to prevent weed competition.
preventive_measures: Monitor canes for cane borers and spur blight.

severity_actions.Healthy: Vigorous and healthy raspberry foliage. Continue routine cane management.

Soybean___healthy.description: Trifoliate leaves are uniform emerald green, well-nodulated roots, and absent of frogeye leaf spots or rust.
cultural_controls: Maintain optimal plant spacing and clean row cultivation.
Ensure proper Rhizobium nodulation.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Encourage natural predators of soybean aphids.
preventive_measures: Perform weekly scouting from R1 through R5 reproductive stages.

severity_actions.Healthy: Crop is healthy. Maintain standard agronomic and soil management.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: White talcum-powder-like fungal growth on upper and lower surfaces of leaves and petioles, leading to premature leaf senescence and sunburned fruit.
cultural_controls: Plant in full sun with wide plant spacing (4-6 feet) to promote airflow.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer which causes dense foliage.
chemical_controls: Apply fungicides such as Trifloxystrobin, Cyflufenamid, or Boscalid + Pyraclostrobin.
biological_controls: Potassium bicarbonate (MilStop, Kaligreen), neem oil, or dilute milk spray (10-20%).
preventive_measures: Plant powdery mildew tolerant or resistant squash hybrids.

severity_actions.Mild: Apply potassium bicarbonate or neem oil spray; prune out heavily covered older base leaves.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply targeted powdery mildew fungicide; ensure coverage of leaf undersides.
severity_actions.Severe: Rotate FRAC fungicide classes every 7 days; protect developing squash fruit from direct sunburn.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Numerous small, irregular purplish spots on upper leaf surfaces that enlarge and cause entire leaves to look scorched, dry, and brown.
cultural_controls: Mow and renovate strawberry beds immediately after harvest, destroying infected foliage.
Avoid overhead watering; use drip tape beneath plastic mulch.
chemical_controls: Apply Captan, Thiram, or Pyraclostrobin early in the season and at post-harvest renovation.
biological_controls: Copper octanoate or Bacillus subtilis foliar bio-fungicides.
preventive_measures: Plant certified disease-free strawberry crowns in well-drained raised beds.

severity_actions.Mild: Remove scorched outer leaves; apply protective copper or Captan spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Captan or Pyraclostrobin; ensure row spacing is weed-free to accelerate drying.
severity_actions.Severe: Post-harvest complete bed renovation and foliage burning; apply systemic fungicide.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Vibrant green trifoliate leaves, healthy crown growth, free of scorch spots or gray mold.
cultural_controls: Maintain clean straw or plastic mulch to keep fruit and leaves off bare soil.
Consistent drip irrigation and balanced potassium feeding.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) for spider mite prevention.
preventive_measures: Regular inspection of crowns and runners.

severity_actions.Healthy: Strawberry bed is healthy. Continue routine mulch maintenance and scouting.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Small (less than 3mm), dark brown to black circular lesions with greasy or water-soaked appearance, surrounded by yellow halos, causing extensive defoliation.
cultural_controls: Do not handle plants or cultivate fields when foliage is wet from dew or rain.
Rotate fields away from tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants for 2-3 years.
Disinfect greenhouse benches, stakes, and tomato cages.
chemical_controls: Apply Copper hydroxide mixed with Mancozeb to enhance bacterial control.
biological_controls: Bacteriophage treatments (AgriPhage) or Bacillus subtilis sprays.
Foliar application of Actigard (acibenzolar-S-methyl) for systemic acquired resistance.
preventive_measures: Use certified disease-free seed and hot-water-treated transplants.

severity_actions.Mild: Prune infected lower foliage with sanitized tools; spray copper + mancozeb or bio-bactericide.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply copper-mancozeb tank mix every 5-7 days; strictly avoid overhead watering.
severity_actions.Severe: Intensive bactericide program; prune damaged branches; isolate affected crop zone.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Brown to black lesions with characteristic concentric target rings starting on older lower leaves, causing yellowing, defoliation, and stem cankers.
cultural_controls: Prune lower leaves (bottom 12-18 inches) once plants reach maturity to prevent soil splash.
Stake and cage plants to keep foliage elevated and dry.
Apply organic or plastic mulch around the base of plants.
chemical_controls: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, Azoxystrobin, or Difenoconazole at first appearance of lower leaf lesions.
biological_controls: Copper fungicides, Bacillus subtilis, or Trichoderma harzianum.
preventive_measures: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Plant early-blight tolerant cultivars (e.g., Mountain Supreme, Defiant PhR).

severity_actions.Mild: Prune out infected lower leaves; apply organic copper or Chlorothalonil spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply systemic Azoxystrobin/Difenoconazole; mulch soil base to eliminate soil splash.
severity_actions.Severe: Spray broad-spectrum fungicide every 7 days; remove severely blighted branches to protect fruit.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Large, irregular, water-soaked oily greenish-gray to dark brown lesions on leaves and stems with white fuzzy sporulation on leaf undersides during cool, moist weather.
cultural_controls: Destroy and bag severely infected plants immediately (do not compost).
Ensure wide plant spacing and drip irrigation exclusively.
Remove nearby volunteer tomato and potato plants.
chemical_controls: Apply specialized oomycete fungicides: Mandipropamid, Dimethomorph, Fluopicolide, or Cymoxanil.
biological_controls: Fixed copper bactericide/fungicide applied preventively before rain events.
preventive_measures: Plant resistant varieties (e.g., Mountain Magic, Plum Regal, Iron Lady).

severity_actions.Mild: Immediate application of Cymoxanil + Mancozeb; inspect entire field daily.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Mandipropamid or Fluopicolide every 5-7 days; prune and bag infected shoots.
severity_actions.Severe: Eradicate heavily infected plants to protect greenhouse/neighboring crops; apply systemic curative fungicide.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Pale greenish-yellow chlorotic spots on upper leaf surfaces matching olive-green to brown velvety fungal patches on lower leaf surfaces; common in high-tunnel greenhouses.
cultural_controls: Reduce relative humidity below 85% in high tunnels using exhaust fans and horizontal airflow.
Increase night temperatures and improve ventilation.
Space plants generously and prune suckers to open canopy.
chemical_controls: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, Difenoconazole, or Cyazofamid.
biological_controls: Copper octanoate, bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis), or potassium bicarbonate.
preventive_measures: Select resistant tomato varieties with Cf resistance genes (Cf-2, Cf-4, Cf-9).

severity_actions.Mild: Turn on high tunnel exhaust fans to lower humidity; remove affected lower leaves; spray copper.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Chlorothalonil or Difenoconazole; prune inner canopy for maximum airflow.
severity_actions.Severe: Implement aggressive humidity management and 7-day fungicide rotation; sanitize greenhouse.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Numerous small (1-3mm) circular spots with dark brown margins and sunken grayish-white centers dotted with tiny black pycnidia.
cultural_controls: Remove diseased bottom leaves promptly.
Mulch soil heavily to prevent rain splash of fungal spores from soil.
Do not overhead water; use soaker hoses or drip irrigation.
chemical_controls: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Pyraclostrobin starting at first sign of symptoms.
biological_controls: Copper soap or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens applied weekly.
preventive_measures: Clean up and burn all crop debris in autumn; practice 3-year crop rotation.

severity_actions.Mild: Pick off spotted lower leaves; apply thick straw/plastic mulch and preventive bio-fungicide.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb fungicide; ensure coverage of lower leaf canopy.
severity_actions.Severe: Fungicide schedule every 7 days; prune lower half of canopy to save upper leaves and fruit.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Fine yellow or white stippling/speckling on leaves, accompanied by fine silky webbing on leaf undersides and shoot tips; leads to leaf bronzing and drying.
cultural_controls: Avoid plant water stress (dusty, hot, drought conditions trigger mite outbreaks).
Wash foliage with strong water spray to knock down mite populations and remove webs.
chemical_controls: Apply selective miticides (Bifenazate, Abamectin, Spiromesifen) rotating chemical modes of action.
biological_controls: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis, Neoseiulus californicus).
Apply insecticidal soaps, neem oil, or rosemary-based horticultural oils.
preventive_measures: Eliminate weeds around greenhouse and field perimeters (which host overwintering mites).

severity_actions.Mild: Spray insecticidal soap or neem oil thoroughly on leaf undersides; release predatory mites.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply targeted miticide (Bifenazate or Abamectin); spray in early morning or evening.
severity_actions.Severe: Rotate between two distinct miticide classes 5-7 days apart; prune heavily webbed shoot tips.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Small pinpoint brown lesions that expand into circular brown spots with concentric light and dark rings and yellow halos; causes extensive foliage collapse.
cultural_controls: Improve air circulation through suckering and proper plant spacing.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Maintain crop hygiene and weed control.
chemical_controls: Apply Azoxystrobin, Fluxapyroxad + Pyraclostrobin, or Chlorothalonil.
biological_controls: Copper hydroxide and bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis).
preventive_measures: Rotate with non-host crops (corn, sorghum); destroy previous solanaceous crop residues.

severity_actions.Mild: Remove affected foliage; apply Chlorothalonil or copper spray.
severity_actions.Moderate: Apply strobilurin/SDHI fungicide; improve canopy ventilation.
severity_actions.Severe: Intensive 7-day fungicide schedule; strip damaged canopy to preserve fruit development.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pathogen_type: Viral (Begomovirus, vectored by Sweetpotato Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Severe upward leaf cupping, curling, yellowing of leaf margins, reduced leaf size (shoestring appearance), flower drop, and stunted bushy growth.
cultural_controls: Install 50-mesh insect screening in high tunnels and greenhouses.
Use reflective silver mulches to repel whitefly vectors.
Immediately rogue and bag symptomatic virus-infected plants.
chemical_controls: Manage whitefly vectors with systemic insecticides (Imidacloprid, Dinotefuran, Spirotetramat, Pyriproxyfen).
biological_controls: Introduce parasitoid wasps (Encarsia formosa, Eretmocerus eremicus).
Apply Beauveria bassiana or insecticidal soap for organic whitefly control.
preventive_measures: Plant TYLCV-resistant tomato cultivars (e.g., Tycoon, Grand Marshall, Red Deuce).

severity_actions.Mild: Immediately rogue and bag symptomatic plants; spray vector control (insecticidal soap or Dinotefuran).
severity_actions.Moderate: Remove all infected plants; apply systemic whitefly insecticide to remaining healthy crop block.
severity_actions.Severe: Eradicate heavily infected section; implement mandatory whitefly eradication protocol across greenhouse/field.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Light and dark green mottled mosaic patterns on leaves, leaf distortion, blistering, fern-leaf growth, and internal browning of fruit.
cultural_controls: Disinfect all tools, stakes, and hands in 20% non-fat dry milk solution or 10% TSP.
Prohibit tobacco use (smoking/chewing) near tomato plants.
Rogue out and destroy infected plants immediately upon symptom detection.
chemical_controls: No chemical virucides exist. Focus entirely on sanitation and vector/contact control.
biological_controls: Use skim milk spray (20%) on workers' hands and tools to inactivate virus particles during handling.
preventive_measures: Plant virus-resistant tomato hybrids (look for 'Tm-2' or 'ToMV' resistance on seed packets).

severity_actions.Mild: Carefully rogue out and bag infected plant; wash hands and tools thoroughly in 20% milk solution.
severity_actions.Moderate: Remove all symptomatic plants; avoid pruning or touching healthy plants without sanitizing.
severity_actions.Severe: Eradicate infected section; sanitize all greenhouse surfaces, soil beds, and irrigation equipment.

Tomato___healthy.description: Foliage is vibrant, deep green, with lush healthy growth, sturdy stems, and no spots, lesions, or curling.
cultural_controls: Maintain consistent drip irrigation (avoid soil dry-wet fluctuations to prevent blossom end rot).
Prune bottom suckers and lower leaves for good ventilation.
Apply balanced organic fertilizer and calcium supplementation.
chemical_controls: None required.
biological_controls: Support beneficial pollinators (bumblebees) and predatory insects.
preventive_measures: Weekly scouting of lower leaves for early blight and leaf mold.

severity_actions.Healthy: Plants are healthy and vigorous. Maintain current irrigation, pruning, and nutrition schedule.
